cues: Permutations, where order matters, are n factorial over n minus r factorial.
Fill restricted places first, tie blocks for together, and use gaps for no two together.
Repeated objects divide by their factorials; circles give n minus one factorial, halved for a garland.
Combinations are permutations divided by r factorial.
And Pascal's rule builds the triangle whose rows add up to powers of two.
